name: Confident AI
tagline: MCP-Native Eval vs Cloud Evaluation Platform
oneLine: An AI quality platform built for enterprise teams to standardize evals and observability; the cloud platform built on top of DeepEval.
tldrVendor: Confident AI is 'the cloud platform built on top of DeepEval', described by the vendor as an AI quality platform built for enterprise teams to standardize evals and observability: LLM-as-a-judge metrics, dashboards and alerting, CI/CD regression testing, dataset generation and curation from production, prompt versioning, and self-hosting on Enterprise plans.

rows.vendor: Python or TypeScript SDKs (deepeval + confident-trace) with a CONFIDENT_API_KEY; OpenTelemetry also supported
rows.quote: Set your project API key as an environment variable

rows.vendor: Managed cloud; Enterprise plans can self-host into your own VPC/VNet via Terraform + Helm (AWS, GCP, Azure)
rows.quote: Self-hosting is available on Enterprise plans.

rows.vendor: Spans via confident-trace decorators or OpenTelemetry in your app; evals run on Confident AI as traces are ingested
rows.quote: in real-time as they're ingested, or retrospectively
Almost all predefined metrics on deepeval use LLM-as-a-judge, with techniques such as QAG (question-answer-generation), DAG (deep acyclic graphs), and G-Eval.

rows.vendor: Automatic or manual token cost per LLM span, per-model pricing lookup; cost per user via user_id
rows.quote: if you provide a supported model on your LLM span and neither SDK-level nor project-level costs are configured, Confident AI will automatically look up the per-token pricing.

rows.vendor: MCP server for coding agents (75 tools: run evals, evaluate traces, simulate conversations); needs Confident AI account
rows.quote: The Confident AI MCP server connects your coding agent to your Confident AI project over the Model Context Protocol

rows.vendor: Proprietary hosted platform on paid plans; the DeepEval framework underneath is Apache 2.0
rows.quote: DeepEval is fully open-source under the Apache 2.0 license and free to use for any purpose.

rows.vendor: Independent; Y Combinator-backed, $2.2M seed (YC, Flex Capital, Vermilion Cliffs, Liquid 2, January Capital, Rebel Fund)
rows.quote: what started off as a bootstrapped open-source package became the thing that got us into YC.

rows.vendor: Agent graph view and user-level analytics dashboards; alerting to Slack, PagerDuty, email
rows.quote: Get notified the moment eval scores drop, latency spikes, or error rates climb. Slack, PagerDuty, email — wherever your team already lives.

rows.vendor: LangChain, CrewAI, OpenAI Agents SDK, LlamaIndex and more; native Python and TypeScript SDKs plus OpenTelemetry
rows.quote: native SDKs for Python and TypeScript and full OpenTelemetry support

rows.vendor: Prompt edits tracked as commits, promoted to versions, labelled (staging/production) and pulled in code by label
rows.quote: Every change you make to a prompt is tracked as a commit. This ensures complete history and traceability of all prompt modifications.

rows.vendor: Team: custom RBAC, SOC2, SSO; Enterprise: dedicated on-prem deployment, HIPAA, custom data residency, 24x7 support

vendorReasons.text: You need team collaboration with shared dashboards and experiments
You want LLM-as-Judge evaluation for nuanced semantic scoring
You need regression testing to compare model versions
You want synthetic dataset generation for comprehensive test coverage
You prefer a managed platform without infrastructure overhead

faq.question: What is the difference between Iris and Confident AI?
faq.vendorPart: Confident AI is the cloud platform built on top of DeepEval that adds centralized test management, observability, collaboration, and analytics. It is a commercial platform (Free, Starter, Team and Enterprise plans), with self-hosting into your own VPC available on Enterprise plans.

faq.question: Should I use Iris or Confident AI for my AI project?
faq.vendorPart: Use Confident AI if you need a managed platform with team collaboration, CI/CD regression testing, dataset curation from production, and LLM-as-a-judge evaluation on every ingested trace.
